French

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Middle French savon, from Old French savon (“soap”), from Latin sāpōnem (“soap”), from Proto-Germanic *saipǭ (“soap”), from Proto-Indo-European *seyb- (“to pour out, drip, strain, trickle”). Cognate with Old English sāpe (“soap”). More at soap.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /sa.vɔ̃/
  • Rhymes: -ɔ̃
  • Audio; “un savon”:(file)
  • Audio (Switzerland (Valais)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
  • Hyphenation: sa‧von

Noun

[edit]

savon m (plural savons)

  1. soap

  • savonneux

Related terms

  • saponaire

  • savonnière

Descendants

[edit]
  • → Hebrew: סבון (sabón)
  • → Malagasy: savony
  • → Koyraboro Senni: saafun
  • → Vietnamese: xà phòng, xà bông
  • → Tai Dam: ꪎꪱꪡ꫁ꪮꪉ
  • → Wolof: saabu
  • → Zarma: saafun

Further reading

[edit]
